data.title: Advanta To Strengthen Market Presence in Africa with Strategic Acquisition of Hytech
data.description:
LONDON, CAIRO and DUBAI, Nov. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Advanta had entered into an agreement on August 15, 2026 to acquire Hytech Egypt USA LLC, the holding company of Misr Hytech Seed International S.A.E. ("Misr Hytech" or the "Company"), from Helios Investment Partners ("Helios") and The Egyptian-American Enterprise Fund ("EAEF") which is advised by Lorax Capital Partners. The transaction has received antitrust approvals from the COMESA Competition and Consumer Commission and the Egyptian Competition Authority and is expected to close on or before January 31, 2027, subject to the satisfaction of the customary closing conditions.

Founded in 1993, Misr Hytech is a leading breeder and producer of proprietary agricultural seeds in Egypt. The Company develops and produces high-quality hybrid seeds across white corn, yellow corn, sorghum and vegetables seeds, and holds the leading market position in Egyptian white corn and sorghum seeds and is a major supplier of yellow corn seeds. Backed by advanced breeding capabilities, proprietary germplasm and integrated production infrastructure, the Company's products reach is approximately 450,000 farmers across Egypt, supported by a network of more than 400 contract production growers. Misr Hytech also has a developing presence in vegetable seeds, complementing its leadership position in field crops. Its advanced breeding program has enabled the development of locally adapted seed varieties with strong yield performance and resilience to regional growing conditions.

The acquisition of Misr Hytech represents a significant strategic step for Advanta, establishing an immediate leadership position in Egypt and creating a strong platform for further growth across the Middle East and Africa. Misr Hytech's established portfolio of proprietary maize and sorghum hybrids, local breeding capabilities, production network and deep relationships with farmers and distributors are highly complementary to Advanta's global R&D, product portfolio and commercial reach.

As part of Advanta, Misr Hytech will retain the local capabilities and relationships that have underpinned its success, while gaining access to broader germplasm, research expertise, seed technologies and regional market opportunities. The combined platform will focus on accelerating product innovation, expanding the portfolio, strengthening seed production and supply resilience, and increasing access to high-quality hybrid seeds for farmers in Egypt and selected regional markets.

Mr. Jai Shroff, Chairman and Group CEO, UPL, said: "Seeds are central to UPL's growth agenda, and Egypt is one of the most strategically important agricultural markets in the Middle East and Africa. Misr Hytech adds proprietary germplasm, strong breeding capability and an established farmer base to our global seeds platform, while gaining access to UPL's worldwide research and distribution network. It is a strong fit with our commitment to Reimagining Sustainability across the agrifood value chain."

Mr. Bhupen Dubey, Global Chief Executive Officer, Advanta, said: "Advanta's proposed acquisition of Misr Hytech aims to achieve a major milestone in its growth journey across Africa. Misr Hytech has built an exceptional business with a market-leading position and a highly respected brand in Egypt. By combining its local leadership and innovation with Advanta's global breeding expertise and commercial reach, we will be well-positioned to deliver greater value to farmers while accelerating growth across the region."

Mohamed Elmokadem, CEO at Misr Hytech, said: "Together with the existing shareholders, we have built a strong and successful business, creating a solid foundation for Hytech's continued growth and development. I am proud of what we have achieved and grateful for the partnership and commitment that have brought us to this important milestone. Joining Advanta marks an exciting new chapter for Hytech, opening up significant opportunities to leverage global expertise, accelerate innovation, and expand our impact across the seed industry. I am confident that the business is well positioned to realize its full potential in this next phase of growth."

Nitin Kaul, Misr Hytech Chairman and Partner at Helios Investment Partners, said: "This transaction marks the culmination of our seven-year partnership with one of the largest independent seed companies in Africa. Over that time, we have worked closely with Misr Hytech's management team to strengthen the business, build a more resilient production model and position the Company for long-term growth. We are proud of the impact that Misr Hytech continues to have supporting and increasing the resilience of small-scale farmers in Egypt."

About UPL

UPL Limited (, BSE: 512070, LSE GDR: UPLL) is a global provider of sustainable agricultural products and solutions that cover the entire agrifood value chain. With annual revenue approximately $6 bn, UPL is one of the largest agriculture companies worldwide, serving growers in more than 140 countries. UPL comprises of four pure-play platforms that include UPL Corporation Ltd (UPL Corp); UPL Sustainable Agri Solutions Ltd. (UPL SAS); Advanta Enterprises Ltd; and SUPERFORM Chemistries Ltd. Together, these platforms are dedicated to Reimagining Sustainability and driving progress in the world. For more information, please visit www.upl-ltd.com.

About Advanta

Advanta is a global agricultural-solutions company with a portfolio of advanced hybrid seeds and post-harvest solutions. The global seeds platform operates a diversified portfolio of over 900 hybrid seed varieties across 40 crops with seeds distributed in more than 70 countries. It combines proprietary germplasm which incorporates over 50 years of research and development, differentiated seed technologies, and global production and distribution. Its post-harvest business is also backed by global reach, product offerings, service and pricing models, including its integrated customer support, dosing and lab testing offerings. Advanta's diverse portfolio includes corn, sorghum, sunflower, canola, rice, and various vegetables, catering to smallholder farmers and commercial farming operations across all five continents, in both developing and developed markets.

About Helios Investment Partners

Helios Investment Partners is a leading Africa-focused private investment firm managing funds totalling over US$ 3 billion. Established in 2004, Helios is led and managed by a predominantly African team, with offices in London, Paris, Lagos and Nairobi, combining deep knowledge of the African operating environment with extensive local and global networks. Helios partners with leading businesses and entrepreneurs to build market-leading companies, bringing capital, operational expertise and a highly engaged approach to value creation.

Since 2004, Helios has applied its investment capabilities, entrepreneurial business-building expertise and local and global connectivity to generate competitive returns and positive impact across Africa. The firm is a certified B Corp, reflecting its long-standing commitment to sustainability and responsible business practices.

About EAEF

The Egyptian-American Enterprise Fund is a privately-managed US government-backed investment fund dedicated to deploying capital into high-potential, private enterprises in Egypt. With a mandate to strengthen Egypt's private sector and deliver competitive returns, EAEF partners with companies and fund managers to scale unique middle-market businesses, enhance operational efficiency, corporate governance, and implement commercial best practices. By attracting foreign investment and supporting entrepreneurial ventures, EAEF plays a key role expanding economic opportunities, fostering market-driven development, and generating strong financial returns.

About Lorax Capital Partners

Lorax Capital Partners is a Cairo-based private equity firm managing investments across Egypt and the broader MENA region. The firm has a strong track record in growth investments, and its team has executed transactions worth more than USD 46 billion. Lorax partners with growth-oriented businesses to create sustainable value through operational improvements, governance enhancement, and strategic development.

data.title: Mahanadi Coalfields IPO: Coal India subsidiary files RHP - Latest GMP at Rs.12.5; check key dates, size, valuation, more
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- Coal India subsidiary Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd (MCL) has filed its Red Herring Prospectus (RHP) for its proposed initial public offering, bringing the public issue closer to launch. The IPO will give investors an opportunity to buy into one of India's largest coal producers, while allowing Coal India to unlock value from the subsidiary through a partial stake sale.

Coal India disclosed the development in an exchange filing on Saturday, November 14. It said, "the Red Herring Prospectus (RHP) dated 13th November, 2026 of Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL), a wholly owned subsidiary of Coal India Limited, was filed with RoC, SEBI, BSE and NSE."

The IPO is scheduled to open on November 19.

Coal India plans to divest up to 10% of its holding through an initial public offering comprising 66.18 crore shares.

The IPO is part of Coal India's strategy to unlock value through subsidiary listings. Bharat Coking Coal was listed in January 2026 and Central Mine Planning & Design Institute in March. South Eastern Coalfields has also filed draft IPO papers and is awaiting SEBI approval.

The IPO comprises an offer for sale of up to 66,18,36,300 equity shares, with a face value of Rs.2 each. Coal India, the promoter and selling shareholder, will sell the entire stake on offer. There is no fresh issue component.

Its expected to be around Rs.9,500 crore to Rs.10,000 crore (approximately $1 billion). Meanwhile, its estimated valuation is likely to be up to $10 billion (roughly Rs.83,000 crore to Rs.90,000 crore) based on market reports and financial projections.

Since the issue is entirely an OFS, Mahanadi Coalfields will not receive any proceeds. The money, after applicable expenses and taxes, will go to Coal India.

The issue will open on November 19 and close on November 23, 2026. Anchor investor bidding is scheduled for November 18. The tentative allotment date is November 25, while listing is expected on November 27.

The latest reported grey market premium (GMP) is Rs.12.50 per share. GMP is an unofficial indicator and can change before listing. It does not guarantee listing gains.

Since the issue has not declared its price band yet, listing gains can't be estimated yet.

No. The RHP does not disclose the price band or final offer price. Consequently, the IPO's valuation and price-to-earnings multiple cannot yet be calculated. The price band is to be announced ahead of the issue.

The offer includes a reservation of up to 3.31 crore shares for eligible employees and 6.61 crore shares for eligible Coal India shareholders. After these reservations, the net offer comprises up to 56.25 crore shares. Of the net offer, up to 50% is available for QIBs, at least 15% for non-institutional investors and at least 35% for retail individual investors.

SBI Capital Markets, Axis Capital, BOB Capital Markets, IDBI Capital Markets & Securities and IIFL Capital Services are the book-running lead managers. KFin Technologies is the registrar to the issue.

MCL's revenue from operations stood at Rs.30,549.59 crore in FY26, compared with Rs.31,353.02 crore in FY25 and Rs.31,634.35 crore in FY24. Profit attributable to owners was Rs.10,677.74 crore in FY26, against Rs.10,823.58 crore in FY25 and Rs.11,841.37 crore in FY24.

For the six months ended September 2026, revenue rose to Rs.16,093.04 crore from Rs.14,724.54 crore a year earlier. Profit attributable to owners increased to Rs.4,878.57 crore from Rs.4,572.66 crore.

MCL produced 218.31 million tonnes and dispatched 210.74 million tonnes in FY26, making it India's largest single coal-producing company that year. It accounted for 21% of domestic coal production. In FY25, production was 225.17 million tonnes and dispatches stood at 210.45 million tonnes.

The company mined 99.4% of its FY26 coal through mechanised surface miners, supporting its large-scale, low-cost opencast operations.

MCL plans to expand existing mines, develop new mining projects and increase coal beneficiation capacity to supply more washed coal. It is also developing first-mile connectivity facilities, silos, rapid-loading systems and rail infrastructure. The company has identified 12 first-mile connectivity facilities with an aggregate capacity of 240.50 million tonnes per year by FY30.

MCL derives the bulk of its revenue from raw non-coking coal, making its business dependent on demand from the power sector. Its expansion plans also depend on timely environmental and forest clearances, land acquisition, rehabilitation and resettlement, contractor performance and evacuation infrastructure. The company has also cautioned that its coal reserve estimates are based on assumptions and actual reserves and production may differ.

data.title: F1's missing diamond mystery: How a crash involving Christian Klien left a $300,000 stone missing for over 22 years
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- A $300,000 diamond attached to a Formula 1 car disappeared following a crash at the 2004 Monaco Grand Prix. More than 22 years later, the mystery surrounding the precious stone remains unsolved, with former Jaguar Racing officials offering fresh insights into what might have happened to It.

According to BBC Sport, the 1.4-carat diamond was mounted on the nose of Austrian driver Christian Klien's Jaguar during the Monaco Grand Prix on 23 May, 2004. It disappeared after the rookie crashed on the opening lap and has never been recovered.

The diamond was part of a promotional partnership between Jaguar Racing and the Hollywood film Ocean's Twelve, starring George Clooney, Brad Pitt and Matt Damon.

Jaguar was looking to generate publicity at a time when its Formula 1 performances were struggling. Its parent company, Ford, had also decided to withdraw from the sport, leaving the team searching for a potential buyer.

Former team principal Tony Purnell said that his responsibilities had changed during that period.

"My job flipped from primarily running the team to primarily selling the team and finding a new owner or they would shut it down," Purnell told BBC Sport.

After a successful promotional partnership with Terminator 3 at Silverstone in 2003, Jaguar's director of communications Nav Sidhu wanted another film collaboration. He negotiated a deal with Hollywood producer Jerry Weintraub for Ocean's Twelve, whose storyline revolved around stealing a diamond-encrusted Faberge egg.

Jaguar partnered with diamond company Steinmetz to place precious stones on the nose cones of cars driven by Mark Webber and Klien. The diamonds were encased in steel, with a separate, larger stone used for photographs. Their combined value would be around $1 million today.

Webber started the 2004 Monaco Grand Prix from 11th on the grid, while Klien began from 14th in only his sixth F1 race.

On the opening lap, Klien made contact with a Jordan car while exiting the Mirabeau corner before crashing into the barriers at the famous Loews hairpin. The Austrian escaped unhurt, but the front of his Jaguar was damaged and the diamond disappeared.

Sidhu soon received a call from the diamond company asking whether it would get its precious stone back.

"I can't remember what I answered, but it certainly wasn't 'yes'," Sidhu told BBC Sport. He had to wait until the race finished, with 76 laps remaining, before inspecting the damaged car. Sidhu described the wait as feeling like a day and a half.

Several theories emerged, including suggestions that the diamond was fake or that Klien had deliberately crashed his car.

Sidhu dismissed the fake-diamond theory, saying the reputational damage to Jaguar and the company would have been considerable. Purnell also backed its authenticity, recalling that team managing director David Pitchforth had tested it by scratching a window with the stone.

Purnell believes somebody might have picked it up, although he also suggested it could have shattered on impact or been swept away during street cleaning. Sidhu thinks someone may have collected it without realising it came from an F1 car.

He also rejected the suggestion that Klien crashed deliberately. According to Sidhu, repairing the car cost more than the reportedly uninsured diamond. Bringing both cars home and scoring points would have offered greater commercial benefits.

Purnell defended Klien, saying: "He was a young guy, first time, made a mistake, it happens."

The disappearance generated the publicity Jaguar had been seeking. Purnell recalled that media attention shifted from the race result to the missing diamond, despite Jarno Trulli winning the Grand Prix and Webber also retiring.

"No-one mentioned Jarno Trulli winning the Grand Prix, no-one asked how the Jaguars did. No-one was interested that Mark Webber's car broke as well. It was, 'where's the diamond?'" Purnell said.

Jaguar was eventually sold to Red Bull six months later. Purnell believes the publicity helped demonstrate the team's commercial potential.

"I think that helped quite a lot because it buzzed the Jaguar team and showed that huge publicity was possible even if you weren't doing so well," he told BBC Sport.

More than two decades later, however, the whereabouts of the $300,000 diamond remain unknown.

data.title: The oil market is brimming with crude despite tanker attacks
data.description:
More than eight months into the Iran war, smoke continues to billow from oil tankers as Tehran presses ahead with repeated attacks near the Strait of Hormuz.

And yet there’s more than enough crude on the global market.

Saudi Arabia, the de facto leader of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, said it pumped 10.5 million barrels a day in October, a level reached only once since 2022. Iraq and Kuwait also reported big increases, while the United Arab Emirates is now free of OPEC quotas, allowing it to pump as much as it wants. Gulf shipments nudged lower this week, but remain healthy despite a slew of attacks, according to TankerTrackers.com Inc.

The ample supply has added to pressure on oil prices. Futures at one point this week were down almost 25% for the month, easing inflation concerns and offering respite for the global economy. Prices for physical cargoes have also plummeted, as producers compete for customers and exorbitant shipping costs begin to thaw.

The recovery is still precarious. Attacks have killed at least one seafarer this month and spilled oil is washing ashore on the region’s beaches. With shipping under constant threat and Iranian media claiming attacks on navigational equipment near Hormuz, oil flows are erratic and could slow at any moment.

But Emirati officials at a recent conference in Abu Dhabi were keen to stress the resilience of the industry. That ability to keep crude flowing, mirrored across the Gulf, has helped bring West Asia shipments back toward pre-war levels and pushed Brent crude prices below $90 a barrel at one point this week.

“For us national shipping companies, there is no choice,” Khalid Alhammad, president of ship management for Saudi vessel owner Bahri, said at a conference in Dubai. “We still have to go through the Strait of Hormuz. We have to keep moving the energy.”

It’s a remarkable turnaround from some of the worst fears at the outset of the war. Before the conflict, about a fifth of the world’s oil flowed through Hormuz, and analysts warned that a closure could send crude prices above $200 a barrel.

Last week at Adipec, the West Asia’s biggest oil conference, senior executives agreed that crude markets look well supplied heading into 2027, with further price declines potentially easing the fight against inflation, though efforts to rebuild stockpiles depleted during the war could limit how far they fall.

The recovery reached a milestone Friday, when the International Energy Agency said oil supply was outpacing demand for the first time since the war began. Rising production beyond the Gulf has helped cushion global markets, with weekly US crude output topping 14 million barrels a day for the first time and the latest figures from Brazil and Guyana all at records.

The IEA said the shift, alongside a plunge in physical crude prices, suggested the market was “showing tentative signs of rebalancing.”

Pockets of tightness persist. Fuel prices remain far higher than crude, with European diesel trading at about $170 a barrel, for example. Shipping costs are also still historically elevated. Transporting crude from the US to Asia adds roughly 20% to the price of American oil, more than double the premium a year ago.

Yet even those strains have eased. Freight markets remain elevated, but are well below the extremes seen a month ago. US retail gasoline prices have also fallen below $4 a gallon for the first time since July, according to the American Automobile Association.

“The return of supply from the Gulf has depressed prices, coupled with the deflation of the freight bubble,” said Sasha Foss, an analyst at Marex Group’s CSC Commodities. “The market is less stressed than it was, but October was the biggest month for vessel incidents in Hormuz, so there are still risks.”

The rebalancing has come at a cost. Vitol Group, the world’s top independent oil trader, said recently that the Iran war has cut global oil consumption by about 3 million barrels a day, an assessment echoed by other major traders. The market, in other words, is finding its footing partly because the war has sharply curtailed demand across fuels and regions.

China’s crude imports fell about 15% from a year earlier to 9.9 million barrels a day in October. European nations have reported double-digit declines in diesel demand, while US gasoline consumption was marginally lower than a year earlier during the peak summer driving season.

The supply recovery began in earnest over the summer and has gathered pace since then. It shows up in a steady uptick in ship-to-ship transfers in the Gulf of Oman, as traders unload cargoes onto new ships just outside Hormuz as part of a burgeoning shuttle trade.

It has left traders with plenty of cargoes to sell. This week, Abu Dhabi National Oil Co. slashed the price of its flagship crude grade to attract buyers. Saudi Arabia also cut its key oil prices, though the kingdom is selling fewer barrels under long-term contracts than before the war, making its pricing harder to track. Instead, it has increasingly turned to ad hoc sales.

The cuts underscore just how much oil is leaving the Gulf, even as tankers remain under attack.

“The workarounds and the shuttle system have managed to keep these prices from going sky-high,” said John Kilduff, partner at Again Capital. “There’s a question of durability. We’ve gone through a period where the Iranians didn’t cause much havoc in the Strait. But lately, that’s ramped up again, and there’s a concern that this could go off the rails.”

data.title: Indonesian president orders greater share of mining benefits for the state
data.description:
Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto said on Saturday that the state should secure a greater share of benefits from all mining permits and, if necessary, hold controlling stakes in mining assets.

  • "From now on, all mining permits, at least 70% must benefit the state. If necessary, the shares should be state-controlled," he said in a speech to members of one of Indonesia's largest Islamic groups, Muhammadiyah

  • A statement from the presidential palace said the 70% stipulated by the president referred to the proceeds from management of mining permits

  • Prabowo added in his speech that Indonesia was open to investors in the mining sector but "the profits must predominantly go to the Indonesian people"

  • Earlier this year, several local media outlets reported, citing Deputy Energy Minister Yuliot Tanjung, that officials had discussed having the mineral and coal sector adopt a gross-split scheme under which 70% of output would go to the government and 30% to the mine operator

  • However, Energy Minister Bahlil Lahadalia later said in June that the proposal had been dropped following consultations with Prabowo

data.title: NASA's Voyager 1 probe poised to achieve mega-distance milestone
data.description:
Key points:
  • Robotic probe is on the cusp of traversing a light-day
  • That is the distance light travels in 24 hours
  • It amounts to about 16 billion miles (26 billion km)
  • Probe launched in 1977, entered interstellar space in 2012

By Will Dunham

NASA's Voyager 1 has already traveled farther than any other spacecraft from Earth since its launch in 1977. The probe, which exited our solar system years ago and is journeying through interstellar space, is now on the cusp of a remarkable milestone — traversing a light-day, the distance light travels in 24 hours.

A light-day is about 16 billion miles (26 billion km). The US space agency said Voyager 1, flying at almost 38,000 miles per hour (61,000 kph) through the virtual vacuum of space, will reach that distance from Earth on Wednesday at 5:16 a.m. ET (1016 GMT). The robotic spacecraft has the distinction of being the most distant human-made object.

"I view it as an engineering milestone, marking the amazing longevity of Voyager 1 — and also an engineering achievement to be able to communicate with Voyager 1 at its distance," said astrophysicist Alan Cummings, a senior research scientist in the Space Radiation Laboratory at Caltech who has been a Voyager program scientist since 1973.

A light-year may be a more familiar concept for many people, a metric used for vast cosmic distances. It is the distance a particle of light, called a photon, travels in a year — about 5.9 trillion miles (9.5 trillion km). For instance, the closest stars beyond our solar system are the three that make up the Alpha Centauri system, about 4.24 light-years away.

TWIN SPACECRAFT

Voyager 1 and twin spacecraft Voyager 2 were launched 49 years ago, exploring planets in the outer solar system before continuing onward. Voyager 1 was carried into space on September 5, 1977, atop a Titan IIIE-Centaur rocket from Cape Canaveral in Florida 16 days after the launch of Voyager 2, but overtook its twin within months.

"Voyager 1 returned a wealth of new information about Jupiter and Saturn, and their moons," Cummings said.

It discovered a thin ring around Jupiter and two previously undetected Jovian moons, Thebe and Metis. It then spotted five new moons around Saturn as well as a ring called the G-ring.

"Voyager 2 took a different path through the solar system after they launched in 1977, in order to visit Uranus and Neptune. Voyager 2 is on pace to be one light-day away from Earth in nine more years, in November 2035," Cummings said.

Voyager 1 crossed the outer edge of the heliosphere, a protective bubble of particles and magnetic fields produced by the sun, and entered interstellar space in 2012, continuing to collect data.

"It was the first spacecraft to report the energy spectra of galactic cosmic rays (fast-moving energetic particles) at low energies. Those energetic particles are not observable inside the heliosphere because of the push-back by the solar wind. This was the holy grail of low-energy cosmic ray physics," said Cummings, an expert in cosmic rays.

Voyager 2 entered interstellar space in 2018.

'THE BACKBONE OF MY CAREER'

Cummings became part of the Voyager scientific team by accident after a balloon-borne experiment concerning cosmic rays that was the basis of his Caltech doctoral thesis failed to land in northern Canada as planned.

"It went around the world a time and a half, and was eventually captured by the Soviet Union. It landed apparently without the benefit of the parachute and was essentially destroyed," Cummings said.

"It was decided that the experiment was finished, and I was offered a job on the Voyager Cosmic Ray Subsystem (instrument) fairly soon after it began development in 1973. The loss of the balloon was lucky for me as the Voyager mission has been the backbone of my career. I've been working on it and analyzing data from it for 53 years," Cummings said.

He joined the Voyager team at age 29 and is now 82.

Both Voyagers carry a Golden Record, a device intended to communicate Earth's story to any intelligent extraterrestrial beings who may encounter the spacecraft. The phonograph record, a 12-inch (30.5-cm) gold-plated copper disk, contains various images and sounds to convey our planet's culture.

It features music like rocker Chuck Berry's "Johnny B. Goode," Beethoven's Fifth Symphony and Aboriginal songs from Australia, as well as spoken greetings in 55 languages and instructions for locating Earth.

Some experts have subsequently questioned the wisdom of providing directions to our planet, in case covetous hostile beings come across the Golden Record.

"I've heard that concern a little over the years but I never worried about it. It's pretty unlikely the aliens will find it," Cummings said.

data.title: How to Plan a 'Tax Holiday' to Cut Your Lifetime Tax Bill — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Karen Hube

At a time when some of the wealthiest Americans use strategies to drop into low tax brackets and pay no federal income taxes in some years, many folks may wonder: Is it possible to achieve this themselves?

With careful planning, it may be.

Taxpayers have more flexibility to drive down their tax rates than they may think, and it has become even easier thanks to juicier tax deductions ushered in by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) passed last year.

"I call it taking a tax holiday," says Erin Scannell, CEO of Ameriprise's Heritage Wealth Advisors. "It opens up the tax playbook dramatically. People save not just in the year they get their tax rates down, but over their lifetimes because a tax holiday enables strategies that set you up for future tax savings."

The planning involves a three-phase process: reducing taxable income for a tax year; arranging for enough liquidity to support your lifestyle in your low-income year; and putting strategies to work for long-term benefits.

Qualifying for a Lower Rate — Perhaps Even a 0% Rate

The lowest income-tax rate is 10%, applied to taxable income of up to $24,800 for couples filing jointly and $12,400 for singles, but the standard deduction or itemized deductions can offset income and create an effective 0% rate.

To qualify for a 0% capital-gains tax rate, taxable income must be no more than $98,900 for couples filing jointly and $49,450 for single filers. Income over those thresholds falls in the 15% capital gains bracket, and over $613,700 and $545,500 respectively in the 20% bracket.

Remember these thresholds for taxable income, not gross income, says Sherman Standberry, founder and CEO of My CPA Coach. "People with salaries well over $100,000 may not realize they're in range of the 0% capital-gains tax bracket."

A married couple earning $130,000 may assume the 0% bracket is out of reach, but after claiming the 2026 standard deduction of $32,200 for couples filing taxes jointly, they would be eligible.

For taxpayers with high incomes, the standard deduction won't lower taxable incomes enough to qualify for a 0% tax, so they have two options: "Defer income into another year or use deductions to offset your income," Scannell says.

Self-employed or newly retired people have an easier time driving down tax rates because they may have more control over when and how they draw taxable income.

A contractor might defer invoicing into a subsequent year. A retiree who hasn't yet started Social Security or required minimum distributions (RMDs) from deferred retirement accounts can postpone realizing gains and rejigger asset location, so income-producing investments are in tax-deferred accounts.

It can be more challenging for people with regular income, such as payrolled workers, retirees taking RMDs, or investment property owners receiving monthly rent.

"But don't let perfection be the enemy of good planning," says Greg Welborn, principal at First Financial Consulting. "Focus on minimizing taxes. A 0% capital gains rate is great, but don't forget that 15% is better than 20%."

There is a long menu of income-reducing strategies, some of which were enhanced by the OBBBA.

Taxpayers can max out pretax contributions to retirement accounts and health savings accounts (HSAs), and bunch future years' charitable contributions to score a fat deduction.

Those who own a business or rental property can purchase deductible equipment or improvements. Under the OBBBA you can immediately write off 100% of certain costs rather than the 20% originally set for this year.

Seniors may qualify for further deductions such as the OBBBA's new $6,000 deduction for taxpayers 65 and older. This tax break phases out once income reaches $250,000 for joint filers and $175,000 for singles.

Creating Liquidity to Live On

Building a stash of liquidity to live on during a tax holiday may require planning a year or more in advance.

Investors can tap cash-equivalent investments and consider selling stock shares with no or very little appreciation, Scannell says.

Consider a loan. "Some people hate the idea of going into debt for their tax holiday, but when you compare the interest you pay and the tax savings, this often makes sense," Scannell says.

If your living expenses are $100,000 and you borrow that at, say, a 6% rate, that is a $6,000 cost. "But if you took that $100,000 out of your investments you might end up paying a lot more in taxes," Scannell says.

Strategies With Long-Term Tax Benefits

In a 0% capital-gains tax year, selling appreciated stock to diversify or rebalance your portfolio is a priority.

You could even sell and immediately rebuy appreciated investments to give yourself a free step-up in cost basis, says Brian Schultz, a tax partner at Plante Moran.

Wash sale rules require 30 days before and after selling a losing investment before buying it back if you want to use the loss to offset gains. "But there are no equivalent wash-sale rules for gains," Schultz says.

Another move with long-term tax benefits: Convert assets in a traditional IRA to a Roth IRA, which allows future tax-free withdrawals and has no RMDs.

Converted assets are subject to income-tax rates. In a year with an inordinately low or zero effective tax rate, you snag a discount on the tax cost of your conversion.

Write to editors@barrons.com

data.title: CVS says GLP-1s save money when priced below $350 per month
data.description:
Key points:
  • CVS analyzed Aetna records for GLP-1 patients for obesity, diabetes and other conditions for up to three years
  • Health plan sponsors spent $3,900 more per person taking a GLP-1 for three years, even after lower medical costs
  • CVS analysis shows 34% to 42% fewer hospitalizations for patients who take the drugs for three years

By Amina Niasse

CVS Health said employers and other health plan sponsors could break even on GLP-1 drugs if they are priced below $350 per month as reduced use of medical services, such as hospitalizations and emergency room visits, lower spending enough to offset drug costs.

CVS said that an analysis of its Aetna insurance claims data found that across patients with obesity, diabetes or other conditions, the current prices for GLP-1 drugs add to spending because they are too high to be impacted by lower medical costs.

The analysis looked at patients who were newly taking highly popular GLP-1 medicines — which mimic the GLP-1 hormone and reduce appetite — from Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk , and compared them to similar patients who were not taking the drugs.

The drugs included Mounjaro and Ozempic for diabetes and Zepbound and Wegovy for obesity. The analysis covered periods of up to three years, with patients starting the medicines between 2023 and 2025.

The analysis did not break out figures for obesity patients alone.

GLP-1 COVERAGE FALLS OVER COST

Coverage of GLP-1 drugs for obesity is falling as corporations and other health plan sponsors try to bring down premiums expected to be up by over 9% in 2027. About 14% of companies have already dropped or plan to drop the drugs in 2027.

Zepbound and Wegovy can cost about $299 and $349 for cash-pay customers. Employers and other health plan sponsors pay between $617 and $766 monthly for the drugs, according to a 2025 study by the Employee Benefit Research Institute. CVS declined to comment on the average prices paid.

Dr Amy Compton-Phillips, chief medical officer at CVS Health, said that the drugmakers' direct-to-consumer prices suggest they can still profit by charging less than $350 a month, while also helping to lower overall healthcare costs. The United States pays more for healthcare than any other country.

“I hope that we can reach that price sooner rather than later,” she said in an interview ahead of the HLTH USA conference in Las Vegas, where CVS will present the findings on November 15.

The US government agreed on a deal with Lilly and Novo last year to pay $245 per month for injectable GLP-1 weight-loss drugs in an 18-month pilot testing their cost-effectiveness for Medicare beneficiaries aged 65 and older or with disabilities.

HOSPITALIZATIONS FALL

CVS said GLP-1 use for obesity, diabetes or other conditions was associated with 10-12% lower emergency room visits in the first and second year of use. It examined records for 60,000 people during the first year and 20,000 people for a second year.

An analysis of records for 4,000 people still taking the drug after three years showed a decrease in hospitalizations of 34-42%, according to the report.

When looking at spending and savings across those three years, plan sponsors saved $9,400 per person on medical bills, but spent $13,300 more on prescriptions, adding costs of $3,900 per person.

The company, which also operates pharmacy benefit manager Caremark and a network of retail pharmacies it plans to spin off, said the price at which GLP-1s start saving money overall depends on how healthy or sick a patient is.

"An older person with diabetes is going to have a higher risk for hospitalization than a younger person who is obese without diabetes," said Compton-Phillips. "The higher-risk the person is, the quicker you get to a return on investment."

SPRINGBORO, OH - November 14, 2026 (NEWMEDIAWIRE) - Rembrandt Roofing & Restoration, a roofing contractor based at 38 N. Pioneer Boulevard in Springboro, is encouraging Greater Dayton homeowners to address attic insulation and ventilation before winter weather sets in.

Ice dams form when heat escaping from the living space warms the roof deck and melts snow from below. The meltwater runs down to the colder eaves and refreezes into a ridge of ice that traps more water behind it. That water can work under shingles and into the attic, staining ceilings and soaking insulation. Southwest Ohio's frequent freeze-thaw cycles make the pattern especially common.

"Homeowners usually call us about an ice dam after the leak appears," said Wade Walker, president of Rembrandt Roofing & Restoration. "The fix that lasts is keeping heat in the house and moving air through the attic, so the roof stays cold and snow melts evenly."

Rembrandt's attic insulation installation service adds blown-in insulation to reduce the heat that reaches the roof deck, with details at https://rembrandtroofing.com/attic-insulation-installation-in-dayton-oh/. Paired with attic ventilation improvements, outlined at https://rembrandtroofing.com/loft-ventilation/, the attic stays closer to outdoor temperature through the winter.

Gutters also play a role. Clogged or sagging gutters hold water at the roof edge, where it can freeze. The company's gutter repair service corrects slope and secures loose sections so meltwater drains away from the home. More information is available at https://rembrandtroofing.com/gutter-repairs/.

Rembrandt Roofing & Restoration serves Springboro, Dayton, Centerville, Carlisle and surrounding Miami Valley communities. Homeowners can schedule an attic and roof evaluation by calling (937) 353-9711.

data.title: Microsoft confirms global outage resolved, rules out cyberattack
data.description:
Microsoft said it had restored Microsoft 365 services after a global outage disrupted Outlook, Teams and other applications for more than 24 hours, reiterating that the disruption was not caused by a cyberattack.

On Saturday, the company said it had “restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions,” directing customers to incident MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

On Friday, Microsoft said that the outage stemmed from a problem introduced during an earlier network capacity upgrade that emerged after a recent network change. “This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents,” the company said.

The company said it had addressed the underlying issue and restored services gradually, checking stability before proceeding to the next stage. Microsoft apologized for the disruption and said it would publish a full post-incident report once its review is complete.

The outage began Thursday, disrupting access to Exchange Online mailboxes and features linked to Outlook, Teams and Microsoft Copilot. Government agencies in Japan, Singapore and the United States experienced email problems, while connections between Microsoft 365 and AI assistants were also affected.

OpenAI said the Microsoft 365 connector in ChatGPT was operating normally again, while Anthropic also marked its Microsoft 365 connector and Claude for Outlook incident as resolved.

data.title: In Jensen Huang's Ouster, Tech Billionaires See a Mistake-and a Lesson — WSJ
data.description:
By Rolfe Winkler

In Jensen Huang, some of America sees a chief executive who was justly tossed from his company for affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and one of his own employees.

Many of his tech-billionaire peers see a brilliant founder who was railroaded.

Elon Musk, Palmer Luckey, Travis Kalanick and Joe Gebbia are among the Silicon Valley billionaires who have taken issue with Huang's ouster from the company Thursday.

On X, Musk posted that he would sign a petition reinstating Huang. Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao called it a "mistake for Nvidia to let Jensen resign."

Epic Games founder and Chief Executive Tim Sweeney said Huang's exit at the hands of the board evidenced "serious corporate governance issues" and showed an "Apple firing Steve Jobs level of idiocy."

Underpinning the defense of Nvidia's longtime CEO is the idea that company founders who create billions or trillions of dollars in value and invent useful technologies are uniquely irreplaceable, and ownership structures should insulate them from public or shareholder pressure.

Company boards previously threw out Sam Altman from OpenAI, Travis Kalanick from Uber, and Jobs from Apple — examples all cited by Huang's peers in supporting him.

Jobs ultimately returned to Apple 12 years after he was fired. Altman was back at OpenAI in five days. Kalanick never returned to Uber and on Monday he posted his own 12-step guide to counter boardroom coups.

"Jensen made a rookie mistake. He had a board," wrote Telegram founder Pavel Durov on X. "Founders: Don't have a board."

Huang's stake in Nvidia is estimated to be worth about $140 billion, but it only represents 3.6% ownership of the company, making him vulnerable to shareholder and board sentiment. Nvidia was founded in 1993 and went public in 1999, a year before the dot-com bubble burst.

Beginning with Google's initial public offering in 2004, many founders of the most successful startups have employed dual-class share structures to enable themselves to maintain voting control without owning a majority of company equity. The investors and founders argue that such structures protect against activist investors who might raid a company for its cash.

Partners at venture-capital firms such as Andreessen Horowitz and Founders Fund have long argued that the best founders are strong personalities pursuing radical, non-consensus ideas and need protection to deliver them.

Marc Andreessen said in 2012 his firm encouraged all of its founders to organize their companies in ways that made it difficult to remove them. "It is unsafe to go public today without a dual-class share structure," he said.

Critics see supervoting shares as a parting gift by venture investors, who often exit after an IPO, demonstrating they are "founder-friendly" so they can win lucrative deals with the next crop of founders.

Huang's value to Nvidia was evident in the sharp decline in its shares after The Wall Street Journal said the board planned to oust him. At their nadir, the company's market capitalization had fallen by more than $500 billion.

Two months ago, Automattic founder Matt Mullenweg was fired by his board following an employee revolt. Mullenweg, whose company contributes to WordPress publishing software, was back in his chair 33 hours and 20 minutes later.

He said boards should not rush to depose a CEO.

"In the fog of war, where there might be incomplete information, it's helpful to give things a few days before drawing final conclusions," he said.

Some Nvidia investors echoed that sentiment, asking the board to reconsider. "We believe it is in the best interest of all stakeholders, and certainly the shareholders of Nvidia, for the board to pursue a slow, measured, and deliberate process regarding the future leadership of Nvidia that leaves all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang," wrote hedge-fund managers Brad Gerstner of Altimeter and Gavin Baker of Atreides Management.

Write to Rolfe Winkler at Rolfe.Winkler@wsj.com

data.title: Eric Balchunas Calls Nvidia-Driven Market Sell-Off The '280th Nervous Breakdown,' Sees Bitcoin Base In The $60K
data.description:
Key points:
  • Bloomberg's Balchunas said sell-offs like the recent drop in Nvidia were likely "algo-driven."
  • Balchunas said investors in stock exchange-traded funds kept buying through the drop.
  • According to him, Bitcoin was harder to hold through a downturn because it was sentiment-driven.

Bloomberg ETF analyst Eric Balchunas called the latest market sell-off "the 280th nervous breakdown that the markets have had in the past couple of years," on Friday, while saying Bitcoin (BTC) appeared to have found "a nice base somewhere in the 60s."

Unfazed By NVIDIA Selloff

Speaking with Scott Melker on The Wolf Of All Streets podcast, Balchunas said sell-offs like the recent drop in Nvidia (NVDA) tended to be "algo-driven, headline-driven," and possibly, "short-lived." He said he was "unfazed" and called the hit to the AI trade "more like a speed bump," unless earnings were running into "a real problem over the next couple quarters."

Balchunas said investors in stock exchange-traded funds (ETFs) kept buying through the drop. "The Vanguard people, they buy it always," he said. "You cannot shake them." Bitcoin ETFs have not followed the same pattern.

Balchunas estimated year-to-date outflows into the funds at about $1.4 billion. "I mean, it's almost flat. Considering the downturn and the negativity, that's pretty good," he said. "You're treading water in a year."

According to SosoValue data, U.S. Bitcoin ETFs stood at $1.75 billion in net outflows so far this year.

'Elevator Up, Stairs Down'

According to Balchunas, Bitcoin was harder to hold through a downturn because it had no cash flows. However, it was "sentiment-driven," but he added that "with all the bad news thrown at it, it seems to have this nice base somewhere in the 60s."

He described Bitcoin's pattern as the reverse of stocks. "It takes the elevator up and the stairs down," Balchunas said, while stocks take "the stairs up and the elevator down."

Bitcoin’s price was trading at $68,000, down nearly 3% over the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘extremely bearish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘high’ levels over the past day.

Pointing to ETFs as a guide, he also explained that the SPDR Gold Shares fund took about eight years to recover from its early peak before more than doubling. "Once the sentiment turns, though, it can go quickly because there's no new supply," Balchunas said.

His comments came as NVDA shares posted their worst week since April last year, falling about 13%, after Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO on Thursday. Balchunas said only "a real problem" with earnings would change his view.

  • Musk responded to the post, saying the vehicle's availability would eventually expand beyond its initial locations.
  • Tesla announced on Friday that select customers are being invited to purchase Cybercab for personal use at an estimated purchase price of $29,990.

Tesla Inc. (TSLA) CEO Elon Musk has acknowledged that the monthly subscription required to operate the company's Cybercab is currently too expensive, responding to criticism from popular tech YouTuber Marques Brownlee, also known as MKBHD.

Musk suggested that Tesla could bring the fee down significantly, even as the company begins inviting select customers to purchase the fully autonomous vehicle.

Tesla shares declined nearly 2% in Friday’s regular trading, while falling another 1% in the afterhours session.

Musk Responds To MKBHD

Brownlee highlighted several restrictions on the Cybercab's newly launched order page in a post on X, including its invite-only availability, limited delivery locations and mandatory monthly subscription.

"Cybercab order page is live. Invite only. Must accept delivery to one of these cities in Texas. Only operates in those existing geofenced areas. Requires a $300 monthly subscription to operate. One vehicle per customer. ‘Estimated delivery’ December," he wrote.

Musk responded to the post, saying the vehicle's availability would eventually expand beyond its initial locations.

"It will be available nationwide, as we receive regulatory approval," Musk said.

However, he agreed that the subscription fee needed to come down, acknowledging that the current pricing was too high.

"But the monthly fee is too high. Should match the cost of Tesla FSD and connectivity for other models, which is more like ~$115/month," Musk added.

The response suggests Tesla could eventually reduce the Cybercab's monthly operating cost from nearly $300 to around $115, although Musk did not provide a timeline for the potential change.

Tesla Cybercab Costs $29,990, But Comes With A Catch

Tesla announced on Friday that "select customers are now being invited to purchase Cybercab for personal use" at an estimated purchase price of $29,990.

The vehicle also requires a $1,000 nonrefundable deposit and a mandatory $299 monthly subscription to Tesla's autonomous driving software. The company estimates deliveries will begin in December.

The two-door, two-seater vehicle has no steering wheel or pedals and was previously deployed exclusively in Tesla's Robotaxi fleet.

However, personal ownership comes with geographic restrictions. Tesla's fine print specifies that personally owned Cybercabs will only operate "in supported service areas."

Ashok Elluswamy, Tesla's head of AI, said the vehicles will "work unsupervised inside all the same geo locations as" the company's existing Robotaxi service.

The initial offering also comes with another limitation, wherein buyers cannot immediately turn their Cybercabs into commercial robotaxis and earn money through Tesla's ride-hailing network.

Tesla's Robotaxi service began operating Model Y SUVs in Austin, Texas, in June 2025 before expanding to other cities in Texas and Florida.

Meanwhile, Musk has previously promised that Tesla owners would eventually be able to add their vehicles to a larger autonomous ride-hailing network.

What Retail Investors Think Of TSLA Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Tesla trended in the ‘bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

TSLA stock is down 12% year-to-date and 13% over the past 12 months. The S&P 500 ETF (SPY) and the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) are up 12% over the past 12 months.

data.title: FAA Lifts Nationwide Groundstop that Upended Flights— WSJ
data.description:
By Alison Sider, Andrew Tangel and Jacob Passy

Federal officials blamed outdated air-traffic control technology for a four-hour groundstop Friday that disrupted thousands of flights around the country.

The drastic step, in response to intermittent air-traffic radio and radar disruptions nationwide, is likely to ripple for days as airlines scramble to reposition aircraft and crews.

Airlines canceled more than 7,500 flights Friday and have already scrubbed 1,800 more on Saturday. Hundreds of flights either turned back or diverted as airports became gridlocked with too many planes on the ground and not enough room to park.

The problem started late Friday afternoon, as the Federal Aviation Administration halted departures shortly before 4 p.m. Eastern, citing extraordinary circumstances and safety concerns. More than 3,500 planes were in the air when the groundstop was issued.

Officials said flights would resume in a slow, controlled manner, with larger passenger planes being prioritized over smaller aircraft. Once the groundstop ended, officials said the FAA was responsible for the turmoil in the nation's airspace it oversees.

"What we have is an incredibly old air-traffic control system," Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Friday in a press conference at the White House, blaming telecom routers that "actually got overloaded with data."

He used the press conference at the White House to plead with Congress to approve funding to make upgrades, which he estimated to cost $50 billion. Without an air-traffic system overhaul, Duffy said outages could happen again — just as there were in the Northeast in September and around Newark Liberty International Airport last year. "You will have more of these," he said.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters that there was no indication so far the outage resulted from a cyberattack. "There's no reason for the public to be afraid or scared for your loved ones," he said.

Instead, Mullin attributed the outage to the FAA's "putting patches into the system," and that new equipment and technology was "overwhelming the older system."

Friday was one of the worst days this year for flight cancellations, outranked by a sprawling winter storm in January that resulted in more than 11,600 cancellations in one day, according to aviation-data provider FlightAware.

More than 30% of U.S. departing flights were canceled Friday, according to Cirium, another aviation-data firm.

Even with the departure ban lifted, airlines were preparing for a difficult reset. Some had already scrubbed the vast majority of what they'd planned to fly the remainder of Friday.

With departures halted, airports filled up, leaving little room for more planes to land. The schedule disruptions left planes and crew members out of place for their next flights. That will likely create cascading problems into the weekend.

"It's going to take us some time to unwind what's happened," Duffy said. The secretary encouraged college football teams to contact the FAA to make sure their chartered jets can make their weekend games.

At Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, word quickly spread among travelers while ground traffic appeared to suddenly stop on the tarmac late Friday afternoon. By early evening, telecom systems at some FAA air-traffic facilities were coming back online.

The outage appeared to be related to a telecommunications network overseen by L3Harris Technologies, according to government and industry officials. Some industry officials briefed on the matter said there were timing issues affecting data synchronization throughout the network, which handles crucial radio frequencies and radar feeds air-traffic controllers rely on to talk to pilots and keep aircraft safely separated.

An L3Harris spokeswoman didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

United Airlines said it would work with customers to get them to destinations once the issue is resolved. American said: "It will be all hands on deck across American to get customers on their way as soon as possible."

Several airlines issued waivers to allow travelers to rebook flights without penalty. At some airports, including New York's LaGuardia, travelers whose flights were canceled had to wait in long lines to get their checked bags back before they could go home. At Newark airport, security lines were empty as people milled about checking their phones for updates.

John Sturino, a musician who plays the drums, said he is going to miss a percussion convention in Indianapolis because of the flight delay. The Brooklyn native said he was waiting in line to cancel his flight at the Delta lounge desk in LaGuardia Airport and get a refund.

"It wasn't worth staying in the airport," he said.

Sara Garven, 66, was traveling with her husband home to Wisconsin from Sarasota, Fla., when the couple were stranded in Baltimore where they had a layover. Overhead announcements were being made roughly every 30 minutes, she said, but the information was no different from what was available online.

"Some are sprinkling the Friday the 13th component, which isn't really helping," she said. "Our main concern is just getting home safely."

This is the second time in recent years the FAA has taken the extraordinary step of halting all departures across the country.

In 2023, a nationwide groundstop was ordered amid an outage of the FAA's Notice to Airmen system, which provides critical information to pilots. That order lasted for two hours, contributing to more than 1,000 flight cancellations. Before that, the FAA had taken that step in response to the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.

Write to Alison Sider at alison.sider@wsj.com, Andrew Tangel at andrew.tangel@wsj.com and Jacob Passy at jacob.passy@wsj.com
